name: Niche Assets and Further Categories
summary: Deal types outside the main sector playbooks, from Chapter 11: tokenized real-world assets, life sciences and biotech, agriculture/farmland/water, banks and bank-like specialty lenders, SPACs/de-SPACs/PIPEs, theme vehicles (AI, crypto, climate, space SPVs), plus the category-table niches (healthcare services cross-reference, industrials and regulated manufacturing, sports/media/entertainment, shipping and logistics, insurance and specialty finance, franchise businesses, music royalties, sports franchises, art and collectibles, family-office direct deals). Each uses the universal library plus the nearest sector playbook. The spine for every niche: find the one asset that is not what it appears (a token that is a contract not title, a water right that is junior, a milestone with no efforts covenant, falsified lab data, uninsured deposits funding long duration, net cash per share far below $10, a theme vehicle launched at the peak, a guarantee hidden in an auction) and verify it with an independent party before anything else. Several niches (11.11) are not yet researched in the bible; their items list the primary sources to pull and are marked weak.
one_check: In every niche, find the one asset that is not what it appears (a token that is a contract and not title, a water right that is junior, a milestone with no efforts covenant, a government payment that can be swept) and verify it with an independent party before anything else.

subtypes.name: Tokenized real-world assets
subtypes.description: Token is usually a contractual or beneficial claim on an off-chain asset held by an issuer, custodian, trust or SPV, not direct title. Trading speed must match the underlying's redemption speed. Underwrite the underlying with its own chapter.

subtypes.name: Life sciences and biotech
subtypes.description: IP and patent runway, clinical stage and data, FDA pathway, reimbursement; killer-acquisition exit risk; earnouts (over 80% of private pharma deals); data integrity in regulated manufacturing (Akorn).

subtypes.name: Agriculture, farmland and water
subtypes.description: Land and water rights, seniority and curtailment (Colorado River structural deficit), commodity price and offtake, crop and weather risk, insurability. Farmland benchmarks are a GAP.

subtypes.name: Banks, credit unions, fintech and bank-like specialty lenders
subtypes.description: Deposit- or short-term-funded lenders: uninsured share, unrealized losses vs equity, IRRBB, 30-day outflow test, Fed collateral pre-positioning (SVB, Signature); plus loan tape, reserves, funding, licensing.

subtypes.name: SPACs, de-SPACs and PIPEs (cross-reference Chapter 5)
subtypes.description: Net cash per share is the number: $4.10 mean / $5.70 median per $10 share for 2019-2020 mergers.

subtypes.name: Theme vehicles (AI, crypto, climate, space SPVs)
subtypes.description: Thematic launches buy at the top (~30% risk-adjusted underperformance over five years); apply bubble tests.

subtypes.name: Healthcare services (cross-reference Healthcare chapter)
subtypes.description: Licensing, reimbursement and payor mix, Stark/AKS, billing quality; PE nursing-home evidence. Full coverage lives in the healthcare roll-ups library; only Chapter 11 items here.

subtypes.name: Industrials and manufacturing (incl. regulated manufacturing)
subtypes.description: Capex, maintenance backlog, Phase I/II, customer concentration, supply chain, equipment condition; data-integrity audit for pharma/food/devices; union and pension liabilities.

subtypes.name: Sports, media and entertainment
subtypes.description: Rights contracts, revenue durability, talent and key-person risk, residuals and royalties. Thin: primary sources to pull.

subtypes.name: Shipping and logistics
subtypes.description: Asset surveys, charter contracts, counterparty risk, flag and registry, cyclicality. v1 row only; no new findings.

subtypes.name: Insurance and specialty finance
subtypes.description: Not yet researched: NAIC statutory filings and RBC ratios, AM Best methodology, state exam reports. Thin.

subtypes.name: Franchise businesses
subtypes.description: FTC Franchise Rule and FDD (Items 17, 19, 20, 21); no-poach clauses (58% of 2016 agreements). Thin.

subtypes.name: Music royalties and IP catalogs
subtypes.description: CRB Phonorecords IV rates, MLC data, catalog multiples and listed royalty-fund write-downs. Thin.

subtypes.name: Sports franchises
subtypes.description: League ownership and debt rules, leaguewide credit facilities, local media-rights contracts. Thin.

subtypes.name: Art and collectibles
subtypes.description: Auction guarantees and third-party irrevocable bids, title/provenance databases, UCC Article 9 for art lending. Thin.

subtypes.name: Family-office direct deals
subtypes.description: Aggregate exposure across all counterparties, not one prime broker's view (Archegos 2021). Thin.

intake_questions.question: Which niche is this (tokenized RWA, life sciences, agriculture/water, bank or bank-like lender, SPAC/PIPE, theme vehicle, healthcare services, industrials, sports/media, shipping, insurance/specialty finance, franchise, music royalties, sports franchise, art/collectibles, family-office direct)?
intake_questions.why: Sets subtype; each niche also uses the nearest sector playbook (11.0).

intake_questions.question: What is the underlying asset, and which sector library applies to it (real estate, credit, PE, healthcare, energy)?
intake_questions.why: Tokenization and wrappers change the wrapper, not the credit (11.2).

intake_questions.question: Does the exit thesis rely on a strategic acquirer, an earnout or milestones?
Does value depend on water rights, insurance availability, or a government act (lease, appropriation, credit, tariff, market rule)?
intake_questions.why: Water seniority, insurability and policy downside (11.4-11.6).

intake_questions.question: Is the business funded by deposits or short-term money?
intake_questions.why: Triggers the SVB uninsured-deposit and duration test (11.7).

intake_questions.question: Is this a de-SPAC, PIPE or SPAC-adjacent deal, or a thematic vehicle raised after a hype cycle?
intake_questions.why: Net cash per share; theme-launch timing (11.9, 11.10).

intake_questions.question: Is the business regulated manufacturing (pharma, food, devices)?

requests.request: Provide a legal opinion on what right the token conveys (title, beneficial or contractual claim) and its enforceability, including the governing court.
requests.format: Opinion from qualified counsel in the asset's jurisdiction.
requests.why: 'Ownership' language for what is a contractual claim.
requests.pass: Right clearly defined and enforceable against the asset holder.
requests.fail: Ownership claimed but only a contractual claim exists; enforceability unclear.

requests.request: Identify the custodian/trust/SPV holding the asset and provide evidence it is bankruptcy-remote from the sponsor.
requests.pass: Asset held by an independent custodian/SPV; non-consolidation opinion.
requests.fail: Sponsor holds asset on balance sheet.

requests.request: Provide the patent schedule with expiry dates, ownership chain and freedom-to-operate analysis.
requests.why: IP runway too short for the thesis.
requests.pass: Runway covers the value-creation plan; ownership clean.

requests.request: Provide clinical-trial stage, data package and FDA pathway/correspondence.
requests.pass: Stage confirmed; pathway agreed with FDA.

requests.request: Provide water source, seniority (priority date) and curtailment priority for every acre and facility.
requests.why: Junior water rights carried at full value.
requests.pass: Every acre mapped to a right with priority date; junior rights impaired in valuation.

requests.request: Provide uninsured share of deposits/funding (FDIC limit $250,000).
Provide unrealized losses on securities against equity.
Compute net cash per share: cash minus merger costs minus warrant value, over shares (after redemptions, sponsor promote, warrants, fees).
requests.why: Headline EV unreliable; 2019-2020 mergers delivered $4.10 mean / $5.70 median per $10 share.
requests.pass: Net cash per share computed and used for valuation.

requests.request: Compare entry valuation to the sector's own history and to the date the theme peaked in media and fund-launch counts.
requests.why: Thematic launches buy at the top (~30% risk-adjusted underperformance over 5 years).
requests.pass: Entry not at peak; valuation within history.
requests.fail: Wave of new vehicles in theme; entry at peak.

requests.request: Provide an overlap map of likely acquirers' pipelines and the exit thesis dependence on any single strategic buyer.
requests.why: Killer acquisitions (~6%, 6.4% in WP) cluster below HSR thresholds; buyer may shelve the asset.
requests.fail: Exit depends on one overlapping strategic buyer.

requests.request: Provide earnout/milestone terms tested against the drafting checklist: objective definitions with worked examples, efforts standard or fixed spend, buyer reporting/audit rights, acceleration on shelving or sale, expert-not-arbitrator scope, records of efforts.
requests.why: Milestones with no efforts covenant; disputes rise with earnout share and length.
requests.fail: Missing efforts covenant or acceleration triggers.

requests.request: Provide a curtailment case (Colorado River basin) with yield impact of junior-right curtailment.
requests.why: No curtailment case (structural deficit ~4M af/yr; 20%-30% further flow declines projected).

requests.request: Provide water cost per acre-foot for the last five years and stress at post-2026 tiered pricing.
Provide IRRBB: economic value of equity under rate shocks.
requests.why: Basel IRRBB would have flagged SVB 10 quarters early.

requests.request: Provide an LCR-style 30-day outflow test.
Apply Xiong's four-feature bubble test (innovation, frenzied new-investor trading, supply increases, bursts without warning).
Provide redemption mechanics, timing and gates, and secondary-trading terms.
requests.why: Token trades 24/7 on an asset that redeems quarterly (liquidity mismatch).
requests.pass: Trading speed matches redemption speed, or gates disclosed.
requests.fail: Secondary trading faster than redemption with no gate disclosure.

requests.request: Provide oracle design, governance and fallback rules for NAV and collateral prices.
requests.why: A single oracle with no fallback.
requests.pass: Multiple sources with fallback and governance.

requests.request: Provide an independent audit or attestation of the reserves or underlying assets.
Underwrite the underlying asset with its own sector library (real estate, credit) and attach that packet.
requests.why: Tokenization changes the wrapper, not the credit.
requests.pass: Underlying passes its own sector checks.

requests.request: Score the token on the five JFC run-vulnerability features.
requests.fail: Liquidity transformation plus threshold effect plus reactive holders.

requests.request: Provide reimbursement analysis.
Provide all FDA 483s and warning letters with close-out and remediation status.
Provide evidence management has read and responded to internal and external audit reports (board minutes, responses).
requests.why: Akorn's CEO never read audit reports.

requests.request: Provide commodity price exposure, hedges and offtake contracts.
Provide crop yield and weather history.
Provide bindable crop and property insurance quotes for the hold, not historical premiums.
requests.why: Crop insurance assumed at historical premiums.

requests.request: Benchmark land value and cash rent against USDA NASS Land Values and Cash Rents and NCREIF Farmland Index.
Provide evidence of collateral pre-positioned at the Fed (discount window) and FHLB capacity.
Provide the loan tape for independent audit, loss reserves and methodology.
Provide licences and regulatory exam history.
Provide funding stability: sources, tenor and concentration.
Provide sponsor promote, warrant terms and redemption levels.
Provide staffing ratios and CMS Five-Star trend after any acquisition.
requests.why: PE nursing homes: mortality up ~10%-11%, frontline staffing down ~3%.
requests.pass: Staffing and ratings stable or improving.

requests.request: Provide fees and leases paid to related parties or landlords, and rent coverage after any sale-leaseback.
requests.why: Costs shifted to fees, interest and leases.

requests.request: Provide licensing, payor mix, Stark/AKS compliance and billing-quality review (government payors ~75% of revenue in nursing homes).
Provide Phase I and Phase II environmental reports.
Provide capex history, maintenance backlog and equipment condition survey.
Provide customer concentration and supply-chain dependencies.
requests.pass: No single customer dominant or contracted.

requests.request: Provide union contracts, open grievances and pension/withdrawal liability estimates.
Provide all rights contracts (media, sponsorship, distribution) with terms and renewal dates.
Provide talent and key-person agreements.
Provide residuals and royalty obligations schedule.
Provide independent asset (vessel) surveys and class records.
Provide charter contracts and charterer credit.
Provide flag and registry documents.
Provide NAIC statutory filings and RBC ratios, AM Best rating reports, and state insurance department exam reports.
requests.pass: RBC above regulatory action levels; no adverse exam findings.

requests.request: Provide the Franchise Disclosure Document (Item 19 FPR, Item 20 outlet turnover, Item 21 audited financials).
requests.pass: Turnover and FPR support the model.

requests.request: Review FDD Item 17 and franchise agreements for no-poach and wage-fixing clauses.
requests.why: 58% of 2016 major franchisor agreements had no-poach clauses; AG and class action exposure.

requests.request: Provide catalog income history tied to MLC data and CRB Phonorecords IV mechanical rates, and benchmark multiple against listed royalty funds' NAV disclosures and write-downs.
Provide chain of title for compositions and masters.
Provide league constitution ownership and debt rules, league approval requirements and leaguewide credit facility terms.
requests.why: League rules restrict control and leverage.

requests.request: Provide title and provenance searches (stolen-art and provenance databases) and UCC Article 9 lien searches.
Disclose auction-house guarantees and third-party irrevocable bids behind comparable sales used for valuation.
Provide aggregate exposure across ALL counterparties and prime brokers, not one broker's view.
For every revenue line depending on a government act (lease, appropriation, credit, tariff, market rule), name the act, the date it could change and the modelled downside.
For any government lease, provide early-termination and termination-for-convenience rights and the exercise case; cap single-agency share of NOI.
requests.why: DOGE listed 793 federal leases for cancellation (2025).

requests.request: Commission an independent data-integrity audit of quality systems: raw lab data vs reported data, audit trails, FDA submissions.
Commission expert scientific diligence.
Commission water-rights counsel opinion on seniority and curtailment priority.
Commission an independent loan-tape audit.
Commission a legal opinion on token rights and bankruptcy remoteness.
Draft specific closing conditions or indemnities for every known regulatory issue rather than relying on a general MAE.
Provide quarterly uninsured-deposit share, unrealized losses, EVE and 30-day outflow metrics.
Provide quarterly earnout/milestone efforts reports and buyer audit-right exercise.
Provide annual water-right status and curtailment notices.
Provide monthly reserve/underlying-asset attestations and redemption queue data for tokens.

kill_tests.test: Token holders hold only a contractual claim against a non-bankruptcy-remote sponsor, marketed as ownership.
Data integrity cannot be verified (raw lab data does not reconcile to reported data) in regulated manufacturing.
Junior water rights carried at full value with no curtailment case in an over-allocated basin.
Unrealized securities losses exceed equity, or uninsured funding concentration with no 30-day outflow coverage.
De-SPAC/PIPE valued on headline EV with no net-cash-per-share computation.
Family-office counterparty refuses aggregate exposure across all brokers.

red_flags.flag: 'Ownership' language for what is a contractual claim.
No bankruptcy-remote holder.
Secondary trading faster than redemption with no gate disclosure.
A single oracle with no fallback.
Reserves attested by the sponsor.
Exit thesis dependent on one overlapping strategic buyer.
Milestones with no efforts covenant.
FDA 483s or warning letters not reconciled to remediation.
Management that has not read its own audit reports.
Junior water rights carried at full value.
A farmland or water-dependent thesis in the Colorado River basin with no curtailment case.
Crop insurance assumed at historical premiums.
Insurance expense held flat in a coastal or wildfire market; coverage only from a state insurer of last resort; an indication presented as a bound quote.
High uninsured deposit share; unrealized losses near equity; no collateral pre-positioned at the Fed.
Headline EV used for a de-SPAC.
A wave of new vehicles in the same theme at entry.
PE-owned healthcare with declining staffing and Five-Star ratings, and related-party fees/leases.
No-poach or wage-fixing clauses in franchise agreements.
Comparable art sales backed by undisclosed guarantees or irrevocable bids.
Exposure view from a single prime broker only.
Government lease ETOs not modelled.

metrics.acceptable: ~$29B on public chains (ex ~$300B stablecoins) plus $16.9B Figure Provenance private credit = ~$46B (Apr 2026); from ~$2.9B (2022), ~$12B (end-2024)
~6% of pharma acquisitions (6.4% in WP); up to ~50/yr; cluster below HSR thresholds
Non-life-sciences: ~1 in 5 private deals (15% 2019, peak 30%-37% 2023, ~22% 2024) | life sciences: >80% of private pharma deals, median ~61% of consideration, 3-5 years
Compact 16.5M af/yr vs ~12.5M af/yr flows (2000-2023); ~4M af/yr deficit; Mead/Powell ~1/3 of 2000 levels; 20%-30% further declines projected; ~80% of allocations to agriculture

metrics.metric: Farmland cap rates and cash-rent yields
metrics.acceptable: GAP: not sourced; pull USDA NASS and NCREIF
2x premium stress; avg homeowner premiums +33% 2020-2023 ($1,902 to $2,530); FL +90%, TX +50% vs 2018; reinsurance ~2x 2017-2023
metrics.source: Keys and Mulder NBER w32579; Yale Insights

metrics.metric: Unrealized loss vs equity (SVB failure level)
metrics.acceptable: SVB ~$17B MTM losses vs $15B equity; losses must be well below equity
Basel IRRBB would have flagged SVB 10 quarters before failure; LCR would have forced tens of billions more liquidity 4+ quarters before
$4.10 mean / $5.70 median (Jan 2019-Jun 2020 mergers); $7.50 before redemptions; later deals higher but far below $10 (Harvard Forum critique disputes predictive power)
metrics.source: Klausner, Ohlrogge, Ruan, Yale J. Reg. 2022

metrics.acceptable: ~30% risk-adjusted loss over first five years
Short-term mortality +10%-11%; frontline staffing -3%; govt payors ~75% of revenue
793 federal leases (~9M sq ft) listed 2025, 384 still listed Aug 2025; GSA leases avg 14 years; ETOs after year 5 on 90-120 days; D.C. NOI -5%; junk CMBS ~4% worse; ~$12B CMBS exposure
metrics.source: LaPoint and Choi via Yale Insights

metrics.metric: Insurance RBC, music multiples, sports league debt limits, art guarantees
metrics.acceptable: GAP: not sourced; primary sources to pull listed in 11.11

third_party_reports.report: Legal opinion on token rights, enforceability and bankruptcy remoteness

hard_questions.question: If the issuer fails, what do token holders own and in which court do they enforce it?
hard_questions.good_answer: A named bankruptcy-remote holder, a defined beneficial right, and a governing court, with an opinion.

hard_questions.question: Who holds the asset, and is it off the sponsor's balance sheet?
hard_questions.good_answer: Independent custodian/SPV with a non-consolidation opinion.

hard_questions.question: How long does a redemption actually take, and when can it be gated?
hard_questions.good_answer: Stated timing matching underlying liquidity, gate terms disclosed.

hard_questions.question: Who sets the NAV the token trades on?
hard_questions.good_answer: Independent administrator with multi-source oracles and fallback.

hard_questions.question: Which likely acquirers have an overlapping program, and what happens to our milestones if they shelve this one?
hard_questions.good_answer: An overlap map plus efforts covenant and acceleration on shelving.

hard_questions.question: Show raw lab data against reported data for the pivotal studies.
hard_questions.good_answer: Raw data provided for independent reconciliation.

hard_questions.question: List every 483 and warning letter and its close-out.
What priority date does each water right carry, and what happens to yield if junior rights are curtailed?
hard_questions.good_answer: Per-acre priority mapping and a curtailment case.

hard_questions.question: What did water cost per acre-foot in each of the last five years, and what is the tiered price after 2026?
What is the bound insurance quote today against the pro forma, and what did premiums do over the last three renewals?
hard_questions.good_answer: Bound quote within pro forma and three-year history.

hard_questions.question: What share of funding is uninsured, and what are unrealized losses against equity?
hard_questions.good_answer: Low uninsured share; losses a small fraction of equity; collateral pre-positioned at the Fed.

hard_questions.question: What is net cash per share after redemptions, promote, warrants and fees?
For each revenue line that depends on a government act, what is the act, when could it change, and what is the downside?
hard_questions.good_answer: A policy register with modelled downsides.

failure_cases.what_happened: Fresenius flagged testing/manufacturing deficiencies but signed; whistleblowers led to findings of falsified data and FDA submissions; Delaware Chancery let Fresenius walk under the MAE (first ruling) but noted diligence-disclosed matters were not carved out; Akorn CEO never read audit reports.
failure_cases.check: Independent data-integrity audit; specific closing conditions/indemnities per known regulatory issue.

failure_cases.what_happened: ~94% uninsured deposits; ~$17B MTM securities losses exceeded $15B equity; $42B one-day run.
failure_cases.check: Uninsured share, unrealized loss to equity, IRRBB, 30-day outflow test.

failure_cases.what_happened: Lacked collateral pre-positioned at the Fed.
Mergers delivered $4.10 mean / $5.70 median net cash per $10 share.
~6% of pharma acquisitions bought to shut down overlapping projects.
Family office exposure invisible across prime brokers.
Mortality up ~10%-11%, staffing down ~3%, costs shifted to fees and leases.
failure_cases.check: Staffing ratios, Five-Star trend, related-party fees and leases.
Read ETOs; model exercise; cap agency share.

failure_cases.case: First Brands and Tricolor (cross-ref Chapters 3 and 4)
failure_cases.what_happened: Collateral integrity failures at specialty lenders.
